### Question 1

A. Pour it down the sink

B. Place it in a garbage bin

C. Burn it by igniting with a match

D. Place it in a separate waste container

### Question 4

Sodium chloride dissolves in water according to the following equation.

$$\ce{NaCl(s) <=> Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq)}$$

A saturated solution of \ce{NaCl} in water contains sodium and chloride ions at the following concentrations.

| *Ion* | *Concentration* (mol L^-1^) |
|-------|---------------------------|
| \ce{Na+} | 6.13 |
| \ce{Cl-} | 6.13 |

What is the $K_{sp}$ of sodium chloride?

A. $2.65 \times 10^{-2}$

B. $8.16 \times 10^{-2}$

C. 12.26

D. 37.6

### Question 6

What happens to the concentration of hydrogen ions during this change of pH?

A. It increases by a factor of 3.

B. It decreases by a factor of 3.

C. It increases by a factor of 1000.

D. It decreases by a factor of 1000.

When equilibrium was established, the mixture contained 0.5 mol of \ce{CO(g)}.

What amount of \ce{H2(g)} was present at equilibrium?

A. 0.2 mol

B. 0.4 mol

C. 0.6 mol

D. 1.0 mol

### Question 12

The industrial production of ammonia is represented by the Haber process reaction shown.

$$\ce{N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g)} \quad \Delta H = -91.8 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Factors such as temperature and pressure need to be considered in order to maximise yield.

Which of the following is correct?

A. A lower pressure would result in a higher yield.

B. A higher pressure would result in a higher yield.

C. A lower temperature would result in a lower yield.

D. A higher temperature would result in a higher yield.

| *Test number* | *Test* | *Observations* |

### Question 15

The table gives the heat of combustion of three different alcohols at 25°C.

| *Alcohol* | *Heat of combustion* (kJ g^-1^) |
|-----------|-------------------------------|
| Methanol | 22.68 |
| Ethanol | 29.67 |
| Butan-1-ol | 36.11 |

Which of the following gives the best approximation for the molar heat of combustion of propan-1-ol, expressed in kJ g^-1^?

A. $\left(\frac{22.68 + 29.67 + 36.11}{3}\right)$

B. $\left(\frac{29.67 + 36.11}{2}\right)$

C. $\left(\frac{22.68 + 29.67}{2}\right)$

D. $\left(\frac{3 \times 36.11}{4}\right)$

### Question 16

A solution contains potassium iodide and potassium chloride. It was analysed by performing a precipitation titration using silver nitrate. The titration curve for this reaction is shown, where $pAg = -\log_{10}[\ce{Ag+}]$.

![Precipitation titration curve](images/q16-precipitation-curve.png){width=70%}

Why is this a valid and correct procedure for quantifying the amount of each anion present in the mixture?

A. \ce{AgCl} would precipitate out first, followed by \ce{AgI}.

B. \ce{AgI} would precipitate out first, followed by \ce{AgCl}.

C. Both \ce{AgI} and \ce{AgCl} precipitate out of the solution together.

D. Neither \ce{AgCl} nor \ce{AgI} would precipitate out of the solution.

|   | *Temperature change at time t* | *ΔH of the forward reaction* |
|---|-------------------------------|----------------------------|
| A. | Decrease | + |
| B. | Decrease | − |
| C. | Increase | + |
| D. | Increase | − |

### Question 20

Nitrogen monoxide and oxygen combine to form nitrogen dioxide, according to the following equation.

$$\ce{2NO(g) + O2(g) <=> 2NO2(g)} \quad K_{eq} = 2.47 \times 10^{12}$$

A 2.00 L vessel is filled with 1.80 mol of \ce{NO2(g)} and the system is allowed to reach equilibrium.

What is the equilibrium concentration of \ce{NO(g)}?

A. 0.00 mol L^-1^

B. $4.34 \times 10^{-5}$ mol L^-1^

C. $6.90 \times 10^{-5}$ mol L^-1^

D. $8.69 \times 10^{-5}$ mol L^-1^

### Question 31 (7 marks)

Copper(II) ions (\ce{Cu^2+}) form a complex with lactic acid (\ce{C3H6O3}), as shown in the equation.

$$\ce{Cu^2+(aq) + 2C3H6O3(aq) <=> [Cu(C3H6O3)2]^2+(aq)}$$

This complex can be detected by measuring its absorbance at 730 nm. A series of solutions containing known concentrations of \ce{[Cu(C3H6O3)2]^2+} were prepared, and their absorbances measured.

| *Concentration of* \ce{[Cu(C3H6O3)2]^2+} (mol L^-1^) | *Absorbance* |
|-----------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| 0.000 | 0.00 |
| 0.010 | 0.13 |
| 0.020 | 0.28 |
| 0.030 | 0.43 |
| 0.040 | 0.57 |
| 0.050 | 0.72 |

Two solutions containing \ce{Cu^2+} and \ce{C3H6O3} were mixed. The initial concentrations of each in the resulting solution are shown in the table.

| *Species* | *Initial concentration* (mol L^-1^) |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|
| \ce{Cu^2+} | 0.056 |
| \ce{C3H6O3} | 0.111 |

When the solution reached equilibrium, its absorbance at 730 nm was 0.66.

You may assume that under the conditions of this experiment, the only species present in the solution are those present in the equation above, and that \ce{[Cu(C3H6O3)2]^2+} is the only species that absorbs at 730 nm.

With the support of a line graph, calculate the equilibrium constant for the reaction.

![Graph paper for plotting calibration curve](images/q31-graph-paper.png){width=90%}

\vspace{8cm}

### Question 32 (5 marks)

The ammonium ion content of mixtures can be determined by boiling the mixture with a known excess of sodium hydroxide. This converts the ammonium ions into gaseous ammonia, which is removed from the system.

$$\ce{NH4+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> NH3(g) + H2O(l)}$$

The excess sodium hydroxide can then be titrated with an acid solution of known concentration.

A fertiliser containing ammonium ions was analysed as follows.

- A sample of fertiliser was treated with 50.00 mL of 1.124 mol L^-1^ sodium hydroxide solution and the solution boiled.
- After all of the ammonia was removed, the resulting solution was transferred to a 250.0 mL volumetric flask and made up to the mark with deionised water.
- 20.00 mL aliquots of this solution were titrated with 0.1102 mol L^-1^ hydrochloric acid, giving the following results.

| *Titration* | *Volume HCl* (mL) |
|------------|------------------|
| 1 | 22.65 |
| 2 | 22.05 |
| 3 | 22.00 |
| 4 | 21.95 |

Calculate the mass of ammonium ions in the sample of fertiliser.

### Question 37 (5 marks)

When performing industrial reductions with \ce{CO(g)}, the following equilibrium is of great importance.

$$\ce{2CO(g) <=> CO2(g) + C(s)} \quad K_{eq} = 10.00 \text{ at } 1095 \text{ K}$$

A 1.00 L sealed vessel at a temperature of 1095 K contains \ce{CO(g)} at a concentration of $1.10 \times 10^{-2}$ mol L^-1^, \ce{CO2(g)} at a concentration of $1.21 \times 10^{-3}$ mol L^-1^, and excess solid carbon.

**(a)** Is the system at equilibrium? Support your answer with calculations. **(2 marks)**

\vspace{3cm}

**(b)** Carbon dioxide gas is added to the system above and the mixture comes to equilibrium. The equilibrium concentrations of \ce{CO(g)} and \ce{CO2(g)} are equal. Excess solid carbon is present and the temperature remains at 1095 K.

Calculate the amount (in mol) of carbon dioxide added to the system. **(3 marks)**
